question: What minimum geometry and operational restrictions apply to a bicycle box, and how must optional green pavement be applied?
model_answer: Direct Answer: A bicycle box must be at least 10 feet deep (measured from its upstream edge nearest the motor-vehicle stop line to its downstream edge nearest the crosswalk or intersection) and must contain at least one bicycle symbol marking. If installing the box requires relocating an existing stop line upstream, the signal's yellow change and red clearance intervals must be recalculated and reprogrammed if necessary. Green-colored pavement is optional, but if used it must cover the full limits of the bicycle box; bicycle boxes are among the limited applications where green pavement is permitted. Standards (mandatory): - "If used, the distance from the upstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest to the stop line for motor vehicles to the downstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest the crosswalk or intersection shall be at least 10 feet. At least one bicycle symbol marking (see Figure 9E-12) shall be used in the bicycle box." - "Where an existing stop line for motor vehicles is relocated upstream to install a new bicycle box, the yellow change and red clearance intervals (see Section 4F.17) shall be recalculated and if necessary, reprogrammed to accommodate the length of the bicycle box." - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be used in the full limits of the bicycle box." - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be limited to: A. Bicycle lanes..., B. Extensions of bicycle lanes through intersections..., C. Extensions of bicycle lanes through areas where motor vehicles enter a mandatory turn lane in which motor vehicles must weave across bicyclists in bicycle lanes..., D. Two-stage bicycle turn boxes..., E. Bicycle Boxes (see Section 9E.12), and F. As a background for bicycle detector symbols..." - "Green-colored pavement shall not be: A. Incorporated into electric-vehicle parking stations or parking stalls, B. Incorporated into crosswalks..., C. Used as a background for shared-lane markings..., or D. Used instead of the required markings for bicycle facilities..." - "If used, the pattern of the green-colored pavement supplementing dotted extension lines shall match the pattern of the dotted lines, thus filling in only the areas that are directly between a pair of dotted line segments." Citations: - Section 9E.12 Standard §6 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Standard §7 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Standard §13 (p.1106) - Section 3H.06 Standard §2 (p.626) - Section 3H.06 Standard §3 (p.626) - Section 3H.06 Standard §4 (p.626)
gold_answer: The box must be at least 10 feet from its upstream edge near the motor-vehicle stop line to its downstream edge near the crosswalk or intersection, must include at least one bicycle symbol, and turns on red must be prohibited from the lane containing the box. If green pavement is used, it must fill the full limits of the bicycle box.
